applicability_clarifications.rule: owner-snapshots/<canonical-job-uuid>/<observed-ns>-<uuid32>.json and query-observations/<observed-ns>-<uuid32>.json are audited by the separate raw recorder rule, filtered by exact pytest node; they are intentionally not duplicated as case-root artifact globs.

Only barriers with an exact test-side persisted file are case artifacts. PhaseBarrier socket paths are under TMPDIR and are not retained as case evidence; barrier ordering is additionally asserted by the test and lifecycle journal.

Test-created child stdout/stderr files and runtime-CLI process-logs are private supporting observations. Where not named as exact artifacts, their contents are not an independent success oracle; pytest assertions and process-journal lifecycle oracle govern expected behavior.

Do not require PBSeq for SQL-only cases or any case whose actual scoped list result has no runs. Preserve actual empty SDK result only when the node records one; this does not imply global server-history absence.

Each retained fence is node-addressed by SHA256(node_id UTF-8); its envelope schema is required_keys, while nested SQL evidence semantics are asserted by the originating schema test and retained-fence review.

limitations.claim: Static rules establish only source-derived file presence/format/schema/key links. They do not establish execution, file permissions at runtime, passing assertions, SQL semantics, or final H2 acceptance.
limitations.oracle: The exact 87 pytest node IDs in cases are required independently by the ledger/JUnit gate.

limitations.claim: PBSeq framing and decoded event structure are supplementary raw proof. JUnit/source assertions remain the semantic oracle for each node; a decoded history file alone cannot establish expected transition semantics.
limitations.oracle: scripts/ifpmic_h2_artifacts.py:audit_artifacts returns h2_accepted=false; pytest XML exact-case oracle is separate.

limitations.claim: The fixture-budget scenario exercises a narrow retained-handle test double; it must not be described as an OS subprocess.

Fixture OIDC descriptor/thread identity, TestClient portal/thread liveness, restore exception identity, and fixture unknown ownership are asserted in the originating tests; serialized fixture journal data is not a complete exception or identity trace.

Runtime-exit and startup no-run variants do not have raw workflow history unless their actual Temporal client query ran and returned a result. Empty result evidence is limited to the exact recorded namespace/workflow query.
limitations.oracle: Per-case query-observations from h2_snapshot_evidence.record_query_observation and test assertions.

limitations.claim: Window clock-seam variants use a synthetic test clock and isolated SQL fixture; they do not establish production clock behavior and do not create Temporal history.
The four-role OID recreation case is SQL-only and has no Temporal endpoint or Temporal history.
The hung-driver backend-disappearance timestamp is dynamically observed and bounded by the pinned phase plan; static source and the saved summary do not prove timing in advance.
Connection-level SCRAM failures may not expose PostgreSQL SQLSTATE; raw exception type and HBA rows are preserved, and no non-null SQLSTATE is inferred.

Runner-generated process-journal.jsonl records are an independent lifecycle oracle and are not written by each test case source. Their schema/identity checks are owned by the runner lifecycle validator.
limitations.oracle: scripts/verify_ifpmic_b03_h2_runtime_full.py lifecycle recorder and per-phase lifecycle checks.

limitations.claim: Raw owner snapshots and direct SDK query results are validated separately by the owner/query recorder audit; these machine rules do not treat synthesized test summary fields as a replacement.
